longDescription:
Thirteen reasoning-and-review skills, each a function with one purpose, and dia, the one skill that calls them.

- dia-skopos: before work starts, shows what it would make of your request and the result it is for, lets you choose which of the two to do, and waits for your word.
- dia-techne: does a task for the outcome it serves, the way the field's best practitioners would, and has the result checked by something other than the model.
- dia-emend: one review pass over a draft that fixes what is confirmed and marks what is only suspected.
- dia-ratchet: review rounds that move only on evidence from outside the model, so you know which claims were checked.
- dia-regula: writes or reviews text a model follows (a prompt, instructions, a skill) against four rules.
- dia-negative: internal critique that holds a claim to the standard it states for itself.
- dia-reductio: holds a position against its own commitments and derives any contradiction line by line.
- dia-warrant: finds the unstated rule behind an argument's step and says how far the conclusion can be relied on.
- dia-conjecture: tests a claim about every case against the cases that press it hardest, and repairs it where one counts.
- dia-counterplan: builds the plan your plan's opposite assumptions give, on the same facts, and says which course it would take.
- dia-adjudicate: rules on reports others wrote about a target, point by point against the sources, and says what no report raised.
- dia-elenchus: Plato's elenchus. Asks what you mean by a key idea, one question at a time, and shows where what you agreed to contradicts your definition.
- dia-quaestio: questions an idea one question at a time, then options, a verdict and a brief with one next step.

Start a message with a skill's name to run it; a request that only sounds like a skill starts none. dia alone loads what each skill needs and returns and the rules for handing work to an agent; dia with a target has it criticised by three independent agents and judged by a fourth.

The skills are instructions only and ship no code of their own; they use the tools your session already has.
capabilities: Show what is asked and the result it is for before work starts
Do a task for the outcome it serves, checked outside the model
Review a draft once and fix confirmed defects
Run review rounds in which only outside checks count, with a round cap
Write or review text a model follows against four rules
Critique a claim by its own standard (internal critique)
Hold a position against its own commitments (reductio ad absurdum)
Test how far an argument's reasons carry its conclusion (Toulmin, critical questions)
Test a universal claim by counterexamples and find the condition it needs (Lakatos)
Build the opposing plan from a plan's key assumptions and weigh the two (dialectical inquiry)
Rule on reports others wrote about a target, point by point against sources
Run a Socratic definition dialogue (elenchus) one question at a time
Question an idea, grow options and end in a brief with one next step
Have a target criticised by three independent agents and judged by a fourth
defaultPrompt: dia-reductio remote work always raises productivity
dia-negative our company is flat, so anyone can speak up freely
dia-quaestio I need a weekend side-project idea
